29. 
30. // Adapter defines the API for the P2P layer, used to connect to peers and exchange messages.
31. type Adapter interface {
32. 	core.Diagnosable
33. 	// Configure configures the Adapter. Must be called before Start().
34. 	Configure(config AdapterConfig) error
35. 	// Configured returns whether the system is configured or not
36. 	Configured() bool
37. 	// Start starts the P2P network on the local node.
38. 	Start() error
39. 	// Stop stops the P2P network on the local node.
40. 	Stop() error
41. 	// AddRemoteNode adds a remote node to the local node's view of the network, so it can become one of our peers.
42. 	// If we'll try to connect to the remote node, true is returned, otherwise false.
43. 	ConnectToPeer(address string) bool
44. 	// ReceivedMessages returns a queue containing all messages received from our peers. It must be drained, because when its buffer is full the producer (Adapter) is blocked.
45. 	ReceivedMessages() MessageQueue
46. 	// Send sends a message to a specific peer.
47. 	Send(peer PeerID, message *transport.NetworkMessage) error
48. 	// Broadcast sends a message to all peers.
49. 	Broadcast(message *transport.NetworkMessage)
50. 	// Peers returns our peers (remote nodes we're currently connected to).
51. 	Peers() []Peer
52. 	// EventChannels returns the channels that are used to communicate P2P network events on. They MUST be listened
53. 	// on by a consumer.
54. 	EventChannels() (peerConnected chan Peer, peerDisconnected chan Peer)
55. }
56. 
57. // MessageQueue defines an interfaces for reading incoming network messages from a queue.
58. type MessageQueue interface {
59. 	// Get returns the next message from the queue, blocking until a message is available. When the queue is shutdown
60. 	// it returns nil.
61. 	Get() PeerMessage
62. }
63. 
64. // Peer holds the properties of a remote node we're connected to
65. type Peer struct {
66. 	// ID holds the unique identificator of the peer
67. 	ID PeerID
68. 	// Address holds the remote address of the node we're actually connected to
69. 	Address string
70. }
71. 
72. // String returns the peer as string.
73. func (p Peer) String() string {
74. 	return fmt.Sprintf("%s@%s", p.ID, p.Address)
75. }
76. 
77. // PeerID defines a peer's unique identifier.
78. type PeerID string
79. 
80. // String returns the PeerID as string.
81. func (p PeerID) String() string {
82. 	return string(p)
83. }
84. 
85. // PeerMessage defines a message received from a peer.
86. type PeerMessage struct {
87. 	// Peer identifies who sent the message.
88. 	Peer PeerID
89. 	// Message contains the received message.
90. 	Message *transport.NetworkMessage
91. }
92. 
93. // AdapterConfig contains configuration for the P2P adapter.
94. type AdapterConfig struct {
95. 	// PeerID contains the ID of the local node.
96. 	PeerID PeerID
97. 	// ListenAddress specifies the socket address the gRPC server should listen on.
98. 	// If not set, the node will not accept incoming connections (but outbound connections can still be made).
99. 	ListenAddress string
100. 	// BootstrapNodes contains the addresses of the remote nodes to initially connect to.
101. 	BootstrapNodes []string
102. 	// ServerCert specifies the TLS client certificate. If set the client should open a TLS socket, otherwise plain TCP.
103. 	ClientCert tls.Certificate
104. 	// ServerCert specifies the TLS server certificate. If set the server should open a TLS socket, otherwise plain TCP.
105. 	ServerCert tls.Certificate
106. 	// TrustStore contains the trust anchors used when verifying remote a peer's TLS certificate.
107. 	TrustStore *x509.CertPool
108. }
109. 
110. func (cfg AdapterConfig) tlsEnabled() bool {
111. 	return cfg.TrustStore != nil
112. }
